summary: The repository supports the proposed pure planner, but several contracts are underspecified around anchor normalization, claim/plan races, lane safety, and closure evidence. Existing CLI/MCP/workflow surfaces also mean the implementation must update more than the planner and three markdown twins.

suggestions.title: Define canonical file extraction from about anchors
suggestions.rationale: Issues store mixed `sym:`, file, test, and spec targets in `about`; connected components are not reproducible until symbol-to-file normalization and treatment of non-code targets are specified. `get_context()` currently uses substring matching, which is insufficient as a grouping contract.

suggestions.title: Version the FixPlan JSON contract and make it deterministic
suggestions.rationale: The current CLI emits ad-hoc text and the service exposes untyped dictionaries. Define stable fields for planner version, ordered issues, group IDs, canonical files, lane, and lane rationale; exclude timestamps and filesystem-dependent values so unattended consumers can compare plans byte-for-byte.

suggestions.title: Treat planning as a snapshot, never as a claim
suggestions.rationale: `ready_work()` performs a best-effort sync and returns open rows, while `claim_issue()` performs the authoritative atomic check inside `ledger.claim`. `/sdd-fix` must claim immediately before execution, abort or re-plan when claim returns false, and never close an issue merely because it appeared in an earlier plan.

suggestions.title: Propagate resolved_by through every close surface
suggestions.rationale: `IssueClosedPayload` and index reduction already support `resolved_by`, but `LedgerService.close_issue()`, the CLI, and the MCP `ledger_close` tool omit it. Updating only the service and CLI would leave agent-driven MCP closures unverifiable.

suggestions.title: Prevent arbitrary or duplicate closure in the fix lane
suggestions.rationale: `close_issue()` currently appends a close event and returns true without checking that the issue exists, is open/claimed, or is claimed by the caller. The fix workflow should require a successful claim and close with the claimant plus `resolved_by`; otherwise an agent can silently close work it never fixed.

suggestions.title: Share severity ordering with ready_work and all consumers
suggestions.rationale: The current `ready_work()` preserves database row order and `ledger ready` prints it verbatim; putting `SEVERITY_ORDER` only in the new planner leaves `/sdd-next` and MCP `ledger_ready` nondeterministic. Introduce one ordering key for the closed Literal vocabulary, with deterministic tie-breakers, and reuse it in the service and planner.

suggestions.title: Make fast-lane overrides subject to hard safety constraints
suggestions.rationale: The requirement that `--lane` forces a lane conflicts with merge-safety unless force means only overriding the heuristic. Critical and vulnerability issues should remain ineligible for automatic fast handling, and the workflow must still preserve `/sdd-done` blocker checks; otherwise a fast override can become an unreviewed bypass.

suggestions.title: Use groups for scheduling, not bulk closure or one-change assumptions
suggestions.rationale: A connected component only proves shared anchors, not that all issues have one root cause or should close together. The current snapshot includes issues spanning source, tests, and specs; execute and close each issue independently while using the group only to co-locate work and avoid conflicting edits.

suggestions.title: Test the complete twin contract and concurrent execution paths
suggestions.rationale: `test_ledger_workflow_twins.py` currently checks file existence and keywords, not equivalent `plan-fix` invocation, JSON parsing, claim failure behavior, lane safety, or closure evidence. Add golden planner tests from representative ledger rows, CLI JSON/exit-code tests, concurrent claim tests, and a required three-file `sdd-fix` twin matrix.

suggestions.title: Resolve fast-lane delivery semantics before implementation
suggestions.rationale: The open question about pushing directly to `dev` conflicts with existing workflow rules: `/sdd-done` defaults to a PR, hotfixes targeting `main` must use a PR, and worktrees use canonical branch/base naming. The plan must carry explicit flow/base-branch metadata and should reuse `plan_worktree()` and `ensure()` rather than inventing direct-push behavior.
